title: Moving artificial objects
question: You spot a rake next to your ball in the rough. If you move the rake and your ball rolls slightly, what must you do?

choices.text: Replace the ball with no penalty.
Add a 1-stroke penalty and replace the ball.
Play the ball from where it comes to rest, with no penalty.
Leave the rake where it is and play as it lies.

explanation: If you accidentally move your ball while moving a movable obstruction like a rake, you simply put the ball back with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What to Do if You Move Your Ball Moving a Rake
juniorVersion.question: You see a rake next to your ball in the long grass. You move the rake, and your ball rolls a little bit. What should you do?

choices.text: Put your ball back where it was, no penalty.
Add one shot to your score and put the ball back.
Play the ball from its new place, no penalty.
Leave the rake and hit the ball as it is.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball moves because you moved a rake or something like it, you just put your ball back to where it was. You don’t get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A tool for smoothing the sand in bunkers (sandy areas on the golf course).
An extra shot added to your score for breaking a rule.
The longer grass next to the fairway.
Something you can move, like a rake or a stick, that isn’t part of the course.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children how to carefully lift and move objects like rakes so they understand when and how to put the ball back if needed.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they always get a penalty if the ball moves.
They might also think they have to play the ball from where it rolled to, even if it was moved by a rake.
